Tunisian baccalaureate, French Baccalaureate, or International Baccalaureate (with M.E.S equivalence for nationals holding a foreign diploma) in a scientific field. Our admission procedure: The admission, procedure starts when the candidate fills out the online application form ( https://www.smu.tn/medtech/medtech-quick-application ) and submits a complete file (see below for a complete list of required documents). 1/- Required documents: One certified copy of the baccalaureate diploma with the exam report (and equivalence from M.E.S for nationals holding a foreign diploma). One certified copy of the school reports (the last two years of high school). A recent birth certificate in French. A copy of the CIN (for Tunisians) or the passport (for internationals). Medical record or medical certificate. Recognition certificate of foreign diplomas from the delivered country (for internationals). Optional: Extracurricular activities: internship, volunteering, associations, extra-curricular achievements & awards certificates if earned. Nb: All the submitted documents remain the property of SMU. Incomplete files will not be processed. 2/- Online Application Form: A candidate who wishes to be admitted to MedTech must fill out the online application form at: https://www.smu.tn/medtech/medtech-quick-application 3/- Admission fees: After filling out the application form and submitting the required documents, the candidate must pay the applicable admission fees. 4/- Placement test: The candidate must take the following placement tests: English test: Tunisian students: are required to take our English test. International students: may request to take our English test online if necessary. Native English speakers are exempt from taking our English test. Math test: All applicants are required to take our math placement test. International students may request to take our math test online if they need to. 5/- Interview: Upon validation of the test(s), the Admission Office will contact you to schedule an appointment for your interview. International students may request a virtual interview, if necessary (over teams or an online video conference- webinar). 6/- Final decision: An admission committee examines your application and communicates a final decision within a period not exceeding seven (07) business days. Once admitted, an official email is sent to the candidate as a confirmation of their admission, and the payment of the first term of the tuition fees is required as a confirmation of their enrollment; otherwise, the priority of acceptance could be awarded to another candidate. text: Research Center page Faculty Research Center Research Groups Research Events Marketing Pub Camp Call for Papers MedTech Research White Book About SMU Research Programs SMU Research Groups Areas Of Advance Introduction SMU Research Center aims at enhancing research opportunities, academic excellence, real-world problem solving, as well as knowledge creation and dissemination. The goal of the Research Center is to enable interaction between faculty and visiting scholars, students and industry in order to raise the profile of SMU as a leading Higher Education institution, innovative, and an actor for change. Objectives Ensure that research contributes effectively to the overall mission of SMU. Sustain and strengthen our research environment, initiatives and create opportunities to generate financial support through private grants for research initiatives. Encourage participation and collaboration between our faculty members and with external stakeholders by building bridges with other academic partners, policy making community, business community and the public sphere in general. Activities Research Ecosystem SMU RESEARCH CENTER : BUILDING BRIDGES Between Academia and the Business community : promote relations with business community through applied research to help them making better choices and anticipate future challenges. Research is valuable in convincing companies to change their way of thinking, operating and doing business. Between Academia and the policy-making community : thinking about the economic, social and international contexts. Conduct high quality research on the challenges Tunisia is facing and foster knowledge production and policy making based on the use of technology tools and research methods that combine both qualitative and quantitative instruments. Between Academia and public sphere : inform public debate, question common ideas and common thinking. Across sectors by promoting collective thinking and building strategic communities including a variety of actors: academia, private sector, civil society and public sector. MITACS Mitacs is a Canadian not-for-profit organization that has designed and delivered research and training programs since 1999. It works with industry, academia and both federal and provincial governments to support applied and industrial research-based innovation. It is dedicated to building international partnerships to help strengthen connections, improve economic performance and create jobs. Over the past 20 years, Mitacs has funded more than 20,000 research projects, trained more than 33,000 students and postdocs and supported more than 3,600 international research collaborations. South Mediterranean University (SMU) has established a partnership with one of Mitacs’ exchange programs, namely, Globalink to carry out joint industrial and academic research projects through leading research groups in top-ranked Canadian universities. The partnership includes two exchange initiatives. GRI One is Mitacs Globalink Research Internship (GRI) for undergraduate students at their final years of studies and combined undergraduate/master’s program students enrolled full-time in a Tunisian university. GRI provides an opportunity for top-ranked applicants to participate in a 12-week (between May and October) research internship under the supervision of Canadian university faculty members in a variety of academic disciplines including science, engineering, mathematics, management, humanities and social sciences. Through this program, the student is given the opportunity to participate in professional trainings and interactions with companies for project management and entrepreneurship experiences. The grant is $12,000 CAD (with a $4000 CAD student’s contribution) and covers student airfare, visa fees, medical insurance, living stipend and research costs. For more information about student’s eligibility, application requirements, implementation timeline and other relevant details regarding matching process and evaluation criteria; please visit the following link: https://www.mitacs.ca/en/programs/globalink/globalink-research-internship GRA The second program included in the SMU-Mitacs partnership is Mitacs Globalink Research Award (GRA) . This mobility exchange is not only designated for undergraduate students at their final years of studies, but also for master’s and Ph.D. students and postdoctoral fellows with full-time affiliations in a Tunisian university. The program allows the participants to work on advanced research projects for a period of 12-24 weeks. It is the responsibility of the participants in this initiative to identify and develop research projects under the joint supervision of a Canadian university faculty member and a professor at a Tunisian university. The grant is $6000 CAD (with a $3000 CAD participant’s contribution). Applications to this program should be made through the SMU. For more information about participant’s eligibility, application requirements and other relevant details; please visit the following link: https://www.mitacs.ca/en/programs/globalink/globalink-research-award If you are interested to apply for one of these programs through SMU-Mitacs partnership, please fill in the following form : Form For more details about the application process through the SMU-Mitacs partnership and the exchange mobility between Tunisia and Canada through Mitacs, please contact: Yasmine Guefrachi, Ph. D. (Assistant Professor at MedTech) at yasmine.guefrachi@medtech.tn Research Groups SMU Research groups are built to interact and identify challenges and explore new insights to co-produce high quality research. These groups also bring together faculty and research students with similar research interests to develop ideas, undertake projects and share expertise. The main idea behind the work of these Research groups is to value the contribution of SMU to organizations. They are built to interact and engage with industry, build partnerships, identify challenges and explore new insights to co-produce solutions for them. Contact Research center team: researchcenter@smu.tn SMU Research Center operates through 4 Areas of Advance that are intertwined with areas of education in our three schools: MSB, MedTech and LCI to promote an interdisciplinary approach. While our Schools provide a solid base of knowledge and expertise, our Areas of Advance – all of which have the goal of sustainable development at their core – target complex societal and economic challenges. Sustainable Development Goals (SDGS) There are 17 SDGs and 169 targets in total. While they are all important and interrelated, some are more relevant to our mission at the Research Center than others. This section can identify the specific SDGs and targets that the Research Center is prioritizing under the Areas of Advance, and demonstrate how they align with SMU strategy and goals. Study in Tunisia page About Our Partners Study Abroad Study in Tunisia Welcome to South Mediterranean University: Tunisia, a North African country, in the heart of the Mediterranean with daily connections to major cities throughout the region. By air, Tunis is less than an hour from Rome, two hours from Paris, and between 2 and 3 hours from any other major city within the EU. Tunisia is a diverse and tolerant country, highly educated, open-minded, with a mosaic of cultural backgrounds. It is a known touristic destination for its coastlines but offers much more than that. Politically, it is a vibrant and young democracy with unprecedented freedom for women, including its ranking as the first Arab country to appoint a female Prime Minister. Life in Tunisia Discover the area SMU’s Campus is located in Lac 2, an important financial and diplomatic district. Within 10-15 minutes driving distance from: Sidi Bou Said, La Marsa, La Goulette and Carthage. Ain Zaghouan: a growing residential area. Major supermarkets and shopping centers. Numerous restaurants and nightlife spots. Housing International Programs department offers assistance with accommodation through a private realtor. Getting a Bank Account In order for you to open a bank account, you need the following documents: A copy of your Residency card (Carte de Sejour) A copy of your certificate of registration at SMU A copy of the first page of your passport Living costs Expenses Approximate amount in USD Shared apartment Between 90 and 150 studio Between 180 and 260 Individual housing (northern suburbs) Between 290 and 440 Food Between 90 and 180 Local transportation Around 73 Books and school materials Included in the tuition fees Clothing and personal expenses Depends on the student’s requirements Health SMU Campus has a doctor and a full-time nurse available in the infirmary, SMU also has a partnership with La Rose Hospital (5mins away from campus) for emergencies and on-campus sickness or accidents. For your mental health SMU Advising and Counselling Center is available for all SMU students. Any foreign national intending to enter Tunisia for the purpose of study should: Obtain a Tunisian visa (if applicable) to facilitate entry. Enter Tunisia through only authorized ports of entry. Present a valid passport to the Immigration officer at the port of entry. Declare the purpose of entry into Tunisia and the intended institution of study. Proceed to the designated immigration office after entry and obtain a residency card. Student Parent Faculty Staff Company Alumni

Advising & Counseling Center page Career and Alumni Services Campus Life Financial Aid Advising & Counseling Center SMU Incubator Library & Archives Student Clubs About Services Eligibility SMU’s top priority is the health and wellbeing of its students. Owing to that fact, SMU presents the Advising and Counseling Center (ACC) that provides academic advising and individual counseling to students in need. The ACC is created to help students keep a healthy state of mind and help them in finding proper on-and-off-campus resources. Students are welcome to talk with their counselor about anxiety, depression, academic performance, self-esteem, stress, family issues, uncertainty, etc. Services are provided by a licensed counselor. Individual counseling sessions Individual academic advising sessions Weekly group sessions and / or workshops related to specific topics. Outreach programs to raise awareness about certain mental health and academic issues and improve self-care. The ACC counselor’s duty is to assess the student’s needs and work with them on setting specific and tailored treatment goals. Students will be scheduled for up to 6 weekly sessions per semester, depending on the student’s condition. If a student needs more sessions, they will be referred to as off -campus professionals . After a thorough assessment, the counselor will give professional advice about the student’s concern(s) and will follow up with their progress. The student may be referred to other student support services available at SMU, such as the Career Center, Student Affairs Office, Peer-to-Peer Tutoring, and other services to be tter address students’ specific needs. All SMU students are welcome to receive help from ACC services. Students can be referred to ACC by: Student Affairs office A faculty member A staff member Self-referral Student Parent Faculty Staff Company Alumni

text: Campus Life page Career and Alumni Services Campus Life Financial Aid Advising & Counseling Center SMU Incubator Library & Archives Student Clubs Life at SMU Campus Safety Student Housing Over 1500 students from across the country or abroad are hosted by SMU for the current academic year. Both Students and Staff are of diverse backgrounds, cultural upbringings, beliefs, political views and are from all over the economic spectrum. This diverse population is what makes life at SMU a riveting experience aimed at creating open minded critical thinkers ready to tackle the world. For broader horizons and for a learning experience that does not stop at the doorsteps of the classrooms, the campus features many clubs and associations that provide extracurricular and co-curricular opportunities for students, launching social projects with Enactus, raising funds and donations for those in need with Lions or developing leadership and aiming for peace with AIESEC or wining competitions and bringing back trophies with SMU Sports Club. SMU students are always learning, developing, and most importantly following their passions around and beyond campus. Safety is considered as paramount within SMU. Regardless of SMU’s safe location “Lac2”, the South Mediterranean University is still doing its best to ensure the safety of students and staff. In collaboration with one of the best Tunisian security companies, SMU campus is staffed 24 hours a day, year-round by trained professionals to guard the campus. The dedication to providing a secure and safe environment for the campus community translates in the fact of arming the campus with high quality Surveillance Cameras in each corridor, box, classroom, and yard. Ensuring the SMU community safety is also enacted in the adoption of secure access to campus through ID cards/badges only. We are pouring ourselves into working on smoothing your transition from high school to university and making it a lifetime journey. While SMU does not currently offer university housing, our admission officers, composed of experts, are fully engaged in providing you with the needed information when it comes to: Real estate agencies Transportation Student budget and living expenses Finding a roommate Cultural attractions Visa requirements (if it is applicable for international students) Furthermore, we host a yearly welcoming orientation session before the beginning of the term for students to meet their peers and find potential roommates. SMU Incubator page Career and Alumni Services Campus Life Financial Aid Advising & Counseling Center SMU Incubator Library & Archives Student Clubs About Incubation Program Incubation process SMU Incubator 1st Cohort SMU Incubator Mag Registration for next Cohort SMU Incubator’s 2nd Cohort SMU Incubator 3rd Cohort SMU Incubator 5th Cohort The SMU Incubator present first appeared in September 2019 in order to respond to the community of Leaders of South Mediterranean University (MSB & MedTech). In fact, driven by the spirit of Innovation in a rich entrepreneurial ecosystem, 10% of our students and Alumni are "young women and young men" Pioneers of change and creators of values. Rich in its faculty, skills and experience, South Mediterranean University has chosen to support its ambitious talents, and project leaders in the development and realization of their business ideas. Our SMU Incubator offers a 5-month training course for entrepreneurs in the ideation phase, through workshops, mentoring, coaching as well as access to our MSB & MedTech courses, which will allow them to make 'Pitches' their concept in front of a jury of experts. SMU Incubator offers a unique opportunity for our entrepreneurs to broaden their vision to other markets and geographic territories but also to gain access to funding organizations through a large network of Alumni and Partners. Our Co-working Space, SMU Incubator, aims to be a place for collaboration between the different entrepreneurs of each cohort, by capitalizing on skills, resources, network and business-engineering synergies. Our 1st SMU Incubator experience enabled 11 startups to be successfully certified: ASG, Barbecha, Eat & Fit, Flow, Hezni Maak, Histoire d'une fleur, Medtrip, Myoya, Tchou-Tchou, Unwasted, Wock’t, 5 of them are Start up Act certified. For more information about our Incubator program, you can contact us at: smu.incubator@smu.tn “ Our 1st SMU Incubator experience enabled 11 startups to be successfully certified: ASG, Barbecha, Eat & Fit, Flow, Hezni Maak, Histoire d'une fleur, Medtrip, My Oya, Tchou-Tchou, Unwasted, Wock’t, “ > Context To benefit from the SMU incubator services the startups need to adhere to three conditions. The newly created companies must comply with startup needs (Judicial, Financial, Business, Technical and Logistic), capitalize on SMU’s assets, and contribute with a clear added value to the ecosystem. The incubation process requires the assistance of all SMU stakeholders suc h the Alumni Association and the Research Centre. Application & Selection process Within the first two months prior to the incubation program, entrepreneurs must send their online applications. The applications will be reviewed by the stakeholders and the participants will be selected based on SMU’s priorities. Need assessment process As soon as the entrepreneurs are selected, they will have to pitch their idea in front of the SMU community followed by a Q&A session. The stakeholders will then provide recommendations that are deemed helpful for entrepreneurs . The main aim of this process is to assess the needs of the startups and provide personalized support. > Mentorship Within the first month, throughout a matchmaking event, the entrepreneur will have the opportunity to work with a professional SMU alumnus alongside a dedicated professional coach from the university’s faculty. Training On a weekly basis, throughout an event, entrepreneurs will get together and share startup progress. The event will also include guest speakers that will share their experiences. The incubator will offer, as well, various sessions on topics such as communication or stress management. Bi-monthly workshops The incubator will hold two-day workshops for the entrepreneurs in which topics such as Branding & Positioning; Design Thinking; Business Modelling; Digital Marketing, Public Relations & Growth Hacking; Startup Valuation and Fundraising; Software Development; Intellectual Property; Machine Learning & Artificial Intelligence; User Experience / User Interface, will be discussed. They will also have the chance to work on their ideas with other entrepreneurs and SMU faculty members. Startup special event Once a month, SMU stakeholders and faculty, alongside entrepreneurs, will launch an event to help promote the company and build its community. The event will also be an opportunity for networking and finding potential future stakeholders. Mid-program review By the end of the second month, an evaluation of the progress will be conducted through an event. Throughout the event the entrepreneurs will give a 3-minute pitch of their ideas to an independent jury. The startups might have the opportunity to access a small fund, through a local crowdfunding system, to create prototypes. Demonstration day By the end of the program, which will last 3 to 4 months, the incubator will celebrate the progress of the startups throughout a special event. During this event, entrepreneurs will conduct a 3-minute pitch of their company. The main goal of this event is to increase the visibility of the company and generate leads while easing the fundraising process. > Currently, 5 of the 11 startups are certified startup acts (Hezni Maak, Tchau Tchau, Barbecha, My-Oya, BMMT). These startups are active in diverse industries like Education, Health, Clean Tech, GreenTech, Manufacturing, Marketing & Communication, … As part of our thriving entrepreneurship ecosystem, SMU is aiming to celebrate its students' and Alumni’s voices and uncover their inspiring stories of trials, hope, and success in everyday life. One of the career center’s key responsibilities is to follow up with its students & Alumni. It is done through surveys, in order to showcase their career path in owning and operating businesses all over the world, as well as to learn more about their business profiles. We have recorded through the surveys a rate of 10% of graduate-all programs combined-that embark on entrepreneurship. And, that’s how the idea of creating SMU Incubator was born. Among the startups that participated in the first launch of the SMU incubator event on 16th of September 2020 at SMU campus, 13 have been identified and selected. The Objectives are: To better assess entrepreneurs' needs and provide personalized support to startups, through training sessions and mentorships. Furthermore, 11 out of 13 startups from our SMU Incubator 1st Cohort are certified. And, 5 of them are Start up act certified. If you want to know more about our certified startup’s of the 1st Cohort, and their achievements, you can download the SMU Incubator magazine as follows: Download Catalog > We are very proud to announce that SMU Incubator’s 2nd Cohort has started and 18 Startups were selected for the next stage. 39 Entrepreneurs with different profiles and backgrounds will join us on Campus during the 3-day Bootcamp, starting from tomorrow September 30th. We wish our applicants the best of luck! #SMU #incubator 38 entrepreneurs from 18 different startups participated in this Cohort. 64.10% of them are Male and 35.90% are female. 66.67% are startups from our SMU Community and the rest are external startups. The backgrounds and profiles of this year’s entrepreneurs are very diverse. In fact, some of the backgrounds that they hold are business, engineering, medical, Physics, law etc.. Furthermore, 28.95% of the entrepreneurs are masters’ holders, and 2.63% are PHD takers. We are very proud to have such talented and brilliant people among us in the Bootcamp that started on Thursday, October 30th. It will also last to Saturday October 2nd. Training sessions and workshops will be provided for free by Dr Noomen Lahimer. On Saturday, the Pitch session will be held, during which the entrepreneurs will have the chance to pitch and present their startups in front of our jury members. And, we are very excited and proud to announce that the Jury is composed of: Mme Anissa Allagui: MSB Faculty Mme Sabra Gargouri: CEO & Co-Founder of MedTrip and also one of the entrepreneurs from SMU Incubator’s 1st Cohort and an EMBA Alumna. Mr Raouf Aouadi : P D G and Co-Founder of Maxula Bourse. Mr Hatem Hlaoui: Co-Founder of Maxula Bourse And, Mr Walid BelHadj Amor General Director of Comete Engineering and EMBA Alumnus. We wish the best of luck to our entrepreneurs ! After the pitch session, following the jury members and board decisions, only 19 entreprepreneurs from 12 Startups have been accepted to start SMU Incubator 2nd Cohort journey. 6 of the 11 startups are certified startup act (Dracoss, ASQII and LoDeep,Monsapo, D Carte, Wise Vision). These startups are active in diverse industries like Education, Health, Clean Tech, GreenTech, Manufacturing, Marketing & Communication, … Moreover, SMU Incubator collaborates with SMU Career Center to connect students with startups for internship opportunities and collabrorates with MSB and MEDTECH faculty to launch challenges in the program of our university. MSB Honor Code page About Us Mission-Vision Dean's Message Accreditations & Memberships Our partners Faculty Openings Staff Openings MSB Honor Code MSB HONOR CODE MSB Honor Code affirms the school’s dedication to integrity and trust. The Honor Code sets out the standards of conduct expected of MSB community members, including students, faculty, and staff. It holds individuals and/or groups responsible for the consequences of their actions. MSB places a strong emphasis on (I) academic integrity, (E) ethics and diversity, and (S) social responsibility and active citizenship. This framework is referred to as IES: Integrity: includes honesty, fairness and transparency in all academic processes, and a rejection of all that is related to falsification, misrepresentation or deception. Ethics and diversity: respecting differences in people, ideas, and opinions. Social responsibility and active citizenship: acting ethically and responsibly according to the school's set regulations. MSB is a community of students, faculty, alumni, and staff involved in learning, teaching, research and services engaged in a collaborative educational endeavor. In accordance with MSB mission and the IES framework, all members of MSB community are expected to contribute positively to MSB's social, learning and work environments. Respect, professionalism, civility, diversity, responsibility, and inclusiveness are key values driving MSB's vision. Failure to fulfill these responsibilities may result in the withdrawal of privileges or the imposition of sanctions. Disciplinary measures for students include but are not limited to: Written warning Probation, during which certain conditions must be fulfilled and good behaviour must be demonstrated Payment of costs or compensation for any loss, damage or injury caused by the conduct Issuance of an apology Loss of certain privileges such as eligibility for exchange opportunities, recommendation letters and scholarships or Tuition waivers Restriction or prohibition of access to, or use of, MSB facilities, services, activities or programs Suspension Expulsion Disciplinary measures for staff and faculty include but are not limited to: Warning Written warning Loss of certain privileges Suspension Expulsion Student Parent Faculty Staff Company Alumni
